12 -> 8. THE FLOOR WAS RED IN THE FALLING DIRECTION and carried no `measured_at`, so nothing could say when it stopped being true. Re-measured on a clean detached worktree at the stamped commit -- python odoo/tooling/lint/py_lint.py agromarin --count -- and it reads 8.

WHAT FELL CANNOT BE ATTRIBUTED, and that is the cost of the missing stamp rather than an omission here: with no commit recorded there is no tree to diff the finding set against. The baseline file was last written by 67e25ce241a (2026-08-25); agromarin has moved since and nothing recorded where. A sibling floor's stamp is the SIBLING's commit, recorded through `--update --root agromarin` from a clean detached worktree of that checkout, so it resolves in the repository that was actually measured.

PREVIOUS NOTE, kept because a floor that loses its history costs more than the stamp gains:

13 -> 12. A WAIVER WRITTEN ANYWHERE IN THE STATEMENT NOW COUNTS. No query changed.

`Suppressions.suppresses` looked at the finding's anchor line alone, and the
anchor is where the STATEMENT starts. So of the three places a developer writes a
directive -- on the finding, on the line that opens the statement, on the line
that closes it -- only the first worked, and the other two failed silently: an
ignored directive looks exactly like an absent one.

Three real waivers were inert and are honoured now:

  agromarin  geoengine/models/geo_domain.py:221   opens a wrapped SQL(...), the
             finding is the nested SQL() on 222
  odoo       website/models/ir_module_module.py:703        closes a comprehension
  odoo       website_sale/models/ir_module_module.py:28    closes a wrapped SQL()

Each was written by someone who believed it worked. `_rules.directive_lines`
gives the lines a directive may sit on, and a COMPOUND statement is still one
line, so a directive in a function body cannot silence a finding about the `def`.

The 22 -> 13 before it was the same shape of counting defect, not a fix: one
query-building helper was reported once per call site.
